chapters.title: Architectural Foundation & Execution Mechanics
chapters.content: Nginx is written in C and engineered around a sophisticated, event-driven, asynchronous architecture that fundamentally departs from traditional process- or thread-per-connection models. At its core, a master process manages multiple worker processes, which are typically bound directly to available CPU cores to optimize cache locality and eliminate unnecessary context switching. Each worker operates within a non-blocking event loop leveraging advanced OS-specific mechanisms like epoll on Linux or kqueue on BSD to handle thousands of simultaneous TCP connections concurrently. By decoupling connection handling from heavy synchronous I/O operations, Nginx minimizes memory footprints and maintains exceptionally predictable latency profiles under immense network loads. This design prevents resource starvation and ensures steady memory utilization even when processing massive volumes of slow-loris vectors or high-concurrency keep-alive traffic streams.
